prerequisites: Successful completion of the modules to be completed in the 1st and 2nd semesters according to the study plan.

learning_outcomes.text: Students master the basics and know the diverse possibilities of economical energy use, in its environmentally friendly provision and in its fields of application, as well as in the availability of suitable energy sources (primary and secondary) in various energy forms and in the technologies for meeting energy demand.
Students are able to carry out, interpret and evaluate standard process engineering experiments.
They can practically apply the knowledge gained in lectures and create meaningful documentation.

syllabus_topics: Fluiddynamik in Füllkörperkolonnen (Fluid dynamics in packed columns)
Partikelgrößenanalyse mittels Laserbeugung (Particle size analysis using laser diffraction)
Fossile und erneuerbare Ressourcen (Fossil and renewable resources)
Kohlendioxid und der Treibhauseffekt (Carbon dioxide and the greenhouse effect)
Hauptsätze der Thermodynamik (Main laws of thermodynamics)
Energieverbrauchsstrukturen und Einsparpotentiale (Energy consumption structures and savings potential)
Kohlendioxidabscheidung und –sequestrierung (Carbon dioxide capture and sequestration)
Nutzung erneuerbarer Energieträger (Use of renewable energy sources)

assessment_methods.method: Practical experiments (Antestat, protocols, final discussion) from the Process Engineering Practical course
Written exam or oral exam for Rational Energy Use

assessment_rules: The module examinations must be passed for the credit points to be awarded. The overall performance in the Process Engineering Practical course is assessed based on continuous assessment through preliminary tests, preparation of reports, and a final discussion for each experiment. Additionally, a written exam is administered for the Rational Energy Use course.
